raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add opt-in `structured_output_prefill` for Chat Completions so a continued assistant message can complete a structured output that has already begun. Addresses #64268.

## Claims

- Initialize the request's grammar with the final assistant content before producing its first token mask; preserve the default constraint on newly generated text.
- Support xgrammar, guidance, and outlines for their existing constraint types. Reject incompatible usage and invalid or transformed prefixes before generation.
- Cover streaming, `echo`, independent request states, and grammar rollback after prefix initialization.

## Validation

CPU serving with `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct`, BF16, eager, MRV1; Python sources imported from this checkout. Native CPU extensions came from `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.32.0-x86_64`. Dependencies: torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.19.0, xgrammar 0.2.8, llguidance 1.7.6, outlines_core 0.2.14, pytest 9.1.0.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Same JSON continuation tests on unmodified base `24e80c2614` | 4 failed with `JSONDecodeError`, 2 default-behavior cases passed |
| Chat request validation and real-server continuation tests | 17 passed |
| Real-backend prefix, rejection, state-isolation, and rollback tests | 18 passed |
| Complete existing XGrammar backend suite | 65 passed |
| Additional real-model HTTP cases | 19 passed |
| `vllm bench serve`, 8 requests, concurrency 2 | 8 successful; 8 concatenated outputs parsed as JSON |
| Pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` | Passed |

Regression command on the base worktree, with the new test module supplied from the implementation worktree:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/workspace/.artifacts/pr-worktree \
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 \
NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost \
uv run --active --no-project python -m pytest \
  /workspace/tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat.py \
  --import-mode=importlib -k structured_output_prefill_json_chat -q
```

The four opt-in cases failed while parsing the combined content: `Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes: line 1 column 17 (char 16)`. After applying the change, all six continuation cases pass as part of the 17-test chat selection.

Commands on the PR checkout, using the same CPU environment variables:

```bash
uv run --active --no-project python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat.py \
  -k structured_output_prefill -q
uv run --active --no-project python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py -k prefill -q
uv run --active --no-project python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/structured_output \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_backend_xgrammar.py -q
```

The additional HTTP checks exercise JSON object, JSON schema, regex, choice, and grammar constraints with streaming enabled and disabled, plus empty/complete/Unicode prefixes, truncation rejection, and concurrent requests. The benchmark validates serving correctness; no performance improvement or general model-accuracy claim is made. GPU execution and CUDA Graph configurations have not been tested.

Existing Buildkite steps select both modified suites: `entrypoints-integration-api-server-openai-chat_completion` and the CPU step running `v1/structured_output`.

## Details

`continue_final_message` puts the assistant prefix in the prompt, while the grammar previously began with only the schema. The new flag carries the exact assistant text to grammar initialization. XGrammar consumes it through `accept_string`; guidance and outlines require lossless tokenization without special token IDs. A rendered-prompt suffix check detects template transformations and prompt truncation.

Admission validation uses a separate matcher to return HTTP 400 for invalid prefixes. The engine creates its own request-local matcher; compiler caches are reused. This adds validation/compilation work for opted-in requests. A nonempty accepted prefix also marks structured content as already started for reasoning gating. Beam search and lm-format-enforcer are rejected for this option.

Enable it alongside `continue_final_message: true` and `add_generation_prompt: false`. With default `echo: false`, concatenate the returned content with the assistant prefix. With `echo: true`, the returned content includes the prefix. Usage and backend limits are documented in `docs/features/structured_outputs.md`.

Duplicate-work checks found no open PR referencing #64268 or implementing this opt-in. The existing issue discussion includes another contributor's reproduction and contract discussion; this PR implements option 3 from the report while preserving default behavior.

nodes.body:
Thanks for picking this up! I tested it with the case that led to #64268, llm-d's chunked decode (`--decode-chunk-size`, llm-d/llm-d-router#3642), on CPU with `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct` (PR head `1d9c2dd8`, Python sources on the `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.32.0` image).

- Default behavior is unchanged without the flag.
- With `structured_output_prefill: true`, two-request continuations are valid for `json_object`, `choice`, `regex` and `grammar`. Prefixes ending in a space, a newline, mid-string or mid Unicode word worked, and an invalid prefix returned 400 as described. `echo: true` and streaming also looked right.
- End to end with the real llm-d sidecar (5 tokens per chunk): unchanged, the output is invalid for `json_object`, `json_schema`, `choice` and `regex`. With a 4-line change that sends the flag on later chunks, all four are valid, while unconstrained requests are still chunked. Reproduction with `docker compose`: https://gist.github.com/shiv4289/fd9170d3bdc0274261663247a42d258b

Not tested: GPU, reasoning models, and the guidance/outlines backends.

@shiv4289 Thanks for testing this with llm-d and sharing the repro! Glad it works for your chunked-decode case. My testing has also been CPU-only so far; I don’t have GPU or reasoning-model results yet.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

@@ -60,6 +60,46 @@ request. You may also choose a specific backend, along with
 some options. A full set of options is available in the `vllm serve --help`
 text.
 
+### Continuing an assistant message
+
+Set `structured_output_prefill: true` on a Chat Completions request to apply
+the constraint to the final assistant message's existing text plus the new
+generation. Also set `continue_final_message: true` and
+`add_generation_prompt: false`.
+
+```json
+{
+  "model": "HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct",
+  "messages": [
+    {"role": "user", "content": "Describe Paris as JSON."},
+    {"role": "assistant", "content": "{\"city\":\"Paris\","}
+  ],
+  "continue_final_message": true,
+  "add_generation_prompt": false,
+  "structured_output_prefill": true,
+  "response_format": {"type": "json_object"}
+}
+```
+
+With the default `echo: false`, the returned `content` contains only the new
+text. Concatenate it with the assistant prefill to obtain the constrained
+output. With `echo: true`, `content` includes the prefill. The prefill remains
+part of the prompt for token accounting.
+
+This option supports `xgrammar`, `guidance`, and `outlines`, for constraints
+supported by the selected backend. The final assistant `content` must be a
+string containing only the structured output prefix. A prefix that violates
+the constraint or does not match the end of the rendered prompt is rejected
+before generation. This includes prefixes altered by chat templates or prompt
+truncation. For `guidance` and `outlines`, the prefix must also round-trip
+through the tokenizer exactly and contain no special token IDs.
+
+By default, constraints apply to newly generated text only. For example,
+an assistant prefill of `Here is the JSON:` can precede a newly generated JSON
+object with `structured_output_prefill` left disabled.
+
+### Constraint examples
+
 Now let's see an example for each of the cases, starting with the `choice`, as it's the easiest one:

issue_comments.body:
Thanks for picking this up! I tested it with the case that led to #64268, llm-d's chunked decode (`--decode-chunk-size`, llm-d/llm-d-router#3642), on CPU with `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct` (PR head `1d9c2dd8`, Python sources on the `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.32.0` image).

- Default behavior is unchanged without the flag.
- With `structured_output_prefill: true`, two-request continuations are valid for `json_object`, `choice`, `regex` and `grammar`. Prefixes ending in a space, a newline, mid-string or mid Unicode word worked, and an invalid prefix returned 400 as described. `echo: true` and streaming also looked right.
- End to end with the real llm-d sidecar (5 tokens per chunk): unchanged, the output is invalid for `json_object`, `json_schema`, `choice` and `regex`. With a 4-line change that sends the flag on later chunks, all four are valid, while unconstrained requests are still chunked. Reproduction with `docker compose`: https://gist.github.com/shiv4289/fd9170d3bdc0274261663247a42d258b

Not tested: GPU, reasoning models, and the guidance/outlines backends.

@shiv4289 Thanks for testing this with llm-d and sharing the repro! Glad it works for your chunked-decode case. My testing has also been CPU-only so far; I don’t have GPU or reasoning-model results yet.
